# The generated-module contract

**What a module built through this skill must be, and what checks it.**

`every-workflow-green` 34. A run that finds nothing in the library for what it
was asked offers to build one; this is the shape the thing that comes back has
to have. The clauses below are not advice — `check_generated_module()` reads a
candidate module with `ast` and returns a violation for each one it breaks, and
the interview is not finished while any violation stands.

Every clause names the symbols in **this installation** it depends on, and a
test resolves each of them. That gate exists because the clause this file
replaced named `ToolRuntime` — a LangChain seam this platform does not surface
— and seven green tests never noticed, because all of them asked whether the
words were present rather than whether the thing existed. *Do not promise which
is not possible* binds the checklist as hard as it binds the build.

What a tool can actually reach here: its node's config through
`configure(data)`, the run through `langgraph.config.get_config()`, memory
through `get_store()`, and **graph state not at all** — `BaseTool.run`
validates `**kwargs` into `Args` and calls `_execute(args)`. A design that
needs graph state belongs in a node, not a tool.

---

## 1. `package-own-tools`

**The rule, in the words the developer is handed:**

> it lives in the {package} package's own tools/ folder, beside its workflow.json — never in the installed package

**Why:** `workflows/` is only the convention: the root is resolved per call from OPENSTATEGRAPH_WORKFLOWS_ROOT, then workflows_dir: in openstategraph.yaml, then the checkout, then ./workflows. A brief naming a literal path is wrong for anyone who configured one and wrong inside a wheel — the exact failure workflows_root.py exists to end. 'Never the installed package' is the half that is testable and root-independent.

**Seams it depends on:** `openstategraph.workflows_root:workflows_root`

## 2. `run-seams`

**The rule, in the words the developer is handed:**

> it takes config through configure(data), the run through langgraph.config.get_config(), the run context the workflow declares through openstategraph.run_context(), and memory through get_store() — a tool cannot read graph state

**Why:** The clause this replaced named ToolRuntime, which does not exist in this platform, and seven green tests never noticed because they asked whether the words were present rather than whether the seam was. These are what prebuilt_session and memory.py actually use. run_context() joined them in organisms-first-class 73: it is the per-run channel a workflow declares in settings.context, and it is where an API handle belongs, because it reaches a tool without reaching a model unless the author opted that field into the prompt.

**Seams it depends on:** `openstategraph.abc.tool:BaseTool.configure`, `langgraph.config:get_config`, `langgraph.config:get_store`, `openstategraph:run_context`

## 3. `ladder`

**The rule, in the words the developer is handed:**

> it is a concrete leaf on the existing tool ladder — a BaseTool subclass that implements _execute

**Why:** Interface -> Abstract -> Base -> Concrete, and a free function that happens to be callable is on none of it. Discovery agrees: folder scopes where to look, subclassing decides what counts.

**Seams it depends on:** `openstategraph.abc.tool:BaseTool`, `openstategraph.abc.tool:BaseTool._execute`

## 4. `declared`

**The rule, in the words the developer is handed:**

> it declares its card fields in node_fields and reads exactly those keys in configure

**Why:** Honesty gate 7. A factory reading an undeclared key does not fail — it reads "" forever, and that defect shipped three times before test_data_key_contract made the fourth impossible.

**Seams it depends on:** `openstategraph.abc.tool:ToolField`, `openstategraph.abc.tool:BaseTool.node_fields`

## 5. `no-credential-value`

**The rule, in the words the developer is handed:**

> any credential is named as an environment variable, never a value

**Why:** A package is committed. Gate 13, and the reason the check is a list of known prefixes rather than a rule: ghp_aaaa... is a GitHub token and a legal variable name at the same time.

**Seams it depends on:** `openstategraph.config_file:SECRET_VALUE_PREFIXES`

---

## What the checker cannot see

It reads the module with `ast` and never imports it — discovery imports a
workflow's `tools/` and records that as a known risk, and a gate that must
execute what it is gating is not a gate. So a class that subclasses `BaseTool`
through an alias, or a `data` key assembled at run time, is invisible to it.
The fix is the same one `test_data_key_contract` asks for: keep the key a
string literal at the point of use.

Passing every clause is necessary and not sufficient. The module's own
behaviour tests are extra — and they are never the gate, because an agent that
writes its own tests writes tests it passes.
